full_instruction: Write a fantasy story about a necromancer who takes on a young apprentice against her better judgment. The necromancer's tower is built from the bones of every creature she has ever raised and released. Write the story in past tense. Use a formal, archaic narrative voice. The story must be exactly six sentences long. During the story, reveal that the apprentice sought her out specifically to learn how to bring back a sibling who died years ago. Include the exact sentence "The dead do not forgive; they simply stop asking." End with the necromancer refusing to teach the final spell, choosing instead to adopt the apprentice as her own.

text: Morgana, whose spiraling spire was constructed entirely from the calcified remains of every soul she had once commanded before letting them wander free, grudgingly accepted the trembling young girl who stood at her gate. The novice confessed that she sought ancient forbidden knowledge solely to resurrect a brother lost to the cruel whims of time and rot. "The dead do not forgive; they simply stop asking," Morgana intoned with a voice like grinding stones as she observed the apprentice's desperate eyes. Though she initially turned down the final necrotic incantation that could breach the veil between worlds, she found herself compelled by the girl's raw grief rather than her ambition. Instead of granting the power to summon the departed, the bone-lord decided that the living bond they shared was far more potent than any resurrection ritual. Thus, Morgana formally adopted the child as her own ward, deciding that protecting a living heart was the only true magic worth mastering in this world of dust and silence.

text: In days of yore, the necromancer Vespera reluctantly accepted a trembling twelve-year boy as her apprentice against her better judgment, though his true desperation was revealed when he confessed he sought her dark arts solely to resurrect the sibling he had lost years past. Her towering spire, constructed entirely from the bleached bones of every creature she had ever raised and released, stood as a solemn monument to her philosophy that honoring the dead meant letting them go. The foundation of ribs and the pillars of dragon vertebrae echoed with the hollow footsteps of a boy who feared the very whispers he was meant to command while carrying the weight of his grief, for Vespera knew the dead do not forgive; they simply stop asking. She explained that each skeletal wall was not a prison but a sanctuary where freed souls chose to rest forever as guardians for the next generation, offering him no promise of reversal against this ancient law. Though terrified by the architecture of angelic ribs and serpent-fire, the young apprentice slowly found awe in the warmth of a million goodbyes within the silent tower, realizing his desperate wish could not bend the will of the departed. Thus, the boy learned that under her strict guidance, death was not an end but a sacred beginning for those who had once walked the earth, and when he pleaded for one final forbidden spell to bring his brother back, she firmly refused, declaring instead that he would henceforth be adopted as her own heir to carry on the legacy of life.

text: Elena lives on her drifting island, where she stitches violent tempests into shimmering cloaks for thirsty sailors seeking safe passage through the fiercest gales. A shadowy rival weaver suddenly arrives, claiming that Elena stole the ancient secret of storm-weaving decades ago and sold it to the highest bidder. As the two face each other amidst swirling clouds, the rival reveals he is right; Elena did take the technique when her own teacher grew too frail to teach anyone else. The revelation hangs heavy in the air, yet Elena confesses that she was merely saving a dying art before the last master passed into silence. She admits to weaving with the thread the size of a hurricane's eye, preserving the knowledge so it would not vanish entirely from the world. In the end, her guilt transforms into purposeful dedication as she vows to teach others, ensuring the storm-cloaks continue to protect the seas long after the rival fades away.

text: A rival weaver arrives on Elara's drifting floating island, shouting that he stole the secret of storm-weaving decades ago only to realize his own methods are now too fragile to hold a thread the size of a hurricane's eye. Elara admits he was right about the theft but reveals that without her weaving the storm back together, his ancient art would have died out entirely alongside him. She shows him how she preserved the dying technique by stabilizing his chaotic crimson bolt into a safe utility for sailors, ensuring the secret survives instead of vanishing into silence. The rival stares in shock at the stabilized cloth, understanding that while he started the fire, Elara is the one keeping it from burning down the world. With a final stitch sealing the storm safely, Elara turns back to her loom as the rival silently accepts his role as guardian of the tradition she saved from extinction. The floating island drifts peacefully onward, weaving calm seas and crashing storms into perfect harmony once more with the dying art reborn under her care.

full_instruction: Write a fantasy story about a giant who owes a debt to a village smaller than his own foot. The village sits at the base of a mountain the giant himself hollowed out generations ago. He has spent a decade building them a wall stone by careful stone as repayment. Include the exact word "smallness" somewhere in the text. End with the villagers inviting the giant to live among them instead of at the mountain's edge.

text: For a decade, the colossal giant stacked every stone from his hollowed-out mountain home into a protective barrier for the village that rested safely beneath his own foot. He believed this labor was a necessary penance for a debt he never truly owed, driven only by a desperate need to feel useful and connected. The villagers watched him work in silence until one day they realized that his obsession was not about repayment but an exile from his own immense size. He had mistaken the village's acceptance of his protection for forgiveness, failing to see that his true debt was the smallness he had chosen over belonging. As he finally understood that no amount of stone could fix a heart searching for a place it never truly left, tears carved channels through the dust on his massive cheeks. The entire community stepped forward with open arms, inviting him to leave the mountain's edge and live among them as their own.

text: For ten years, the mountain-sized Oromis quietly built a protective wall stone by careful stone around the village of Kaelen's Hollow to repay a honey debt that was never actually owed, driven instead by a desperate need for belonging where the villagers' smallness offered him a home. Despite his immense strength usually causing destruction, the giant moved with careful precision to ensure no tremor would crack the delicate mud-brick houses carved into his own hollowed flesh because he had nowhere else left to exist but here. A recent storm threatened to collapse the ceiling above them, but Oromis dove down just in time to catch the falling debris gently in his palms while keeping the villagers safe not out of obligation but out of love for their tiny existence. He then produced a small, saved jar of wildflower honey from his belt, an act that seemed like payment for a promise made when a boy once fell onto his tongue, though it was really just a gesture of his need to stay close to their smallness. With the wall complete and the storm broken, the villagers accepted the honey not as settlement of a debt but as a token of gratitude for a giant who stayed because he belonged to them before warmly inviting him to leave the mountain's edge and live permanently among them. The giant bowed low in gratitude, finally free from the burden of an imaginary debt while standing as the permanent shield of the tiny people who gave him a home within his own bones.

full_instruction: Write a fantasy story about an oracle famous across the land for never once telling a lie, told in first person from the oracle's perspective. The temple where she serves has not seen a single visitor leave happy in thirty years. She answers every question asked of her, no matter how cruel the truth. The story must be exactly six sentences long. During the story, reveal that she has been quietly phrasing every true answer to guide people toward the choice that helps them most. End with a child asking her a question she finally cannot bear to answer honestly.

text: For thirty years, my temple has stood as a mausoleum of regret, where no soul has departed with a smile after I delivered the absolute truth to their trembling lips. Though the world calls me cruel for never speaking a lie, I have quietly woven every harsh prophecy with subtle phrasing that gently steers desperate hearts toward the path of least suffering. They think they are victims of my cold honesty, unaware that my words about "certain death" were often coded instructions on how to survive, and my prophecies of "doomed love" were actually warnings to find a kinder companion before it was too late. Today, a small child stands before the stone altar with eyes wide with innocent fear, asking if I can tell her exactly which toy is the most beloved by every single friend in the kingdom. The moment his question hangs in the air, I realize that unlike all my previous answers, this time I cannot bear to guide him away from the hard truth because he is too young to understand the deception yet. With a heavy heart, I must speak the unvarnished reality that his favorite toy is hated by everyone, knowing it will shatter his spirit before I can find the courage to gently steer him toward a different, better friendship.

text: For thirty years, I have sat in my silent temple answering every cruel question with an unvarnished truth, yet I secretly shape those harsh facts into truths that gently steer lost souls toward their own salvation. When Kaelen demanded to know if a lie would bring him magic, I told him the hard fact that no such magic exists, but phrased it so clearly that he immediately understood his only path was to return and save his dying mother instead of spending the stolen gem on greed. Every visitor leaves weeping because my answers are brutally honest, but they are never random; I carefully select the specific true details that force them to realize their own mistakes without ever breaking my vow of absolute veracity. The king who feared defeat left in despair thinking his army would lose, only for me to have phrased my answer about their rotting armor so precisely that he realized his victory lay not in battle but in mercy, a truth he chose to accept too late but one I had guided him toward from the start. Even now, as Kaelen flees into the rain to face his mother's anger, I sit quietly knowing I did not give him hope or comfort, but I phrased my cruel truth about his theft in such a way that he found the strength to choose redemption over self-destruction. Though no smile has ever graced a visitor's face in this temple of pain, I have spent decades quietly weaving guides into every brutal fact, ensuring that even the harshest truth leads them toward the choice that saves their soul, until a small child runs to me with tears streaming down his face and asks, "If I promise never to steal again, will you love me?"
